title: The Speed of Light and Its Significance
text: The speed of light in a vacuum, denoted by the symbol c, is exactly 299,792,458 meters per second (approximately 186,282 miles per second). This value was established as a defined constant in 1983 when the meter was redefined in terms of the speed of light. According to Einstein's special relativity, c is the ultimate speed limit in the universe — no information or matter can travel faster than light. Light from the Sun takes approximately 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth. The constancy of the speed of light regardless of the observer's motion is one of the most tested and confirmed results in physics.
